claims.text: Threshold matter for the record: the three artifacts describe the same trip. The trip_id TRP-00109 appears on the trip record, the GPS trace and the fare breakdown, and the trace's first fix (2026-07-21T18:21:10) matches the trip record's started_at to the second, so the rider's initial burden under limb (a) is discharged on matching identifiers and a matching pickup timestamp.

On the governing trace field the trip covers 13.76 km against a booked optimal of 6.4 km - an excess of 7.36 km, which is 115% of the optimal route. Both POL-RD-01 gates are cleared (more than 0.8 km absolute, more than 20% relative), and because the excess also exceeds 50% of optimal the deviation is additionally MATERIAL, exactly as the trace-derived status records. The rider's limb (b) burden is discharged.

POL-RD-01 makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km the governing measurement and expressly forbids citing trip_record.actual_distance_km for the threshold test. The rider measures on the trace's 13.76 km, and that figure clears the gate by itself, so nothing in this case turns on the rounded 13.8 km convenience copy on the trip record.

The traffic-advisory artifact is MISSING: no advisory covers this corridor on this trip, and absence is citable. I disclose that EV-ADVIS-00109-01 carries weight 0.0, has no payload, and fired the issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT. With no named road or expressway segment, no validity window overlapping the trace, and no matched corridor exit and rejoin, POL-RD-03 exonerates nothing here - the driver has no road-condition answer to the deviation.

Neither of the other baseline-lifting clauses is available to the driver. pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are both null and amended_optimal_distance_km is null, so there is no re-quote for POL-RD-05 to re-run POL-RD-01 against; and vehicle_type is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, so the matched-itinerary baseline of POL-RD-12 never arises. The comparison stays where the rider put it: 13.76 km driven against 6.4 km optimal.

The rider's own message at 18:22:06 asked for a stop - 'stop at jurong point first? need to grab something 5 min'. POL-RD-04 excuses a deviation only 'to the extent' it is attributable to such an instruction: it excludes the excess distance between leaving and rejoining the optimal corridor and nothing beyond that. It does not reclassify the whole 7.36 km excess as a lawful trip, it does not displace POL-RD-01 or POL-RD-02 for any excess left over from the subtraction, and the size of the attributable portion is the driver's to establish under POL-RD-08. The record carries no derived measurement of that portion at all, so the exclusion cannot be shown to consume the rider's whole excess.

The fare model is METERED and quoted_fare_sgd is null, so POL-RD-11 - which would close off the distance refund as one the rider never lost - does not apply. If the deviation stands, the remedy is POL-RD-02 arithmetic and not discretion: charged_total 21.32 less a recomputed fare of 13.32 (base 3.80 + 0.75 x 6.4 km + 0.28 x 14.0 min, surge multiplier 1.0 read from the fare breakdown, plus the 0.80 platform fee), giving a refund of 8.00. That is above the 0.50 de minimis floor and short of the 90% full-refund share, so it is a PARTIAL_REFUND of 8.00, not the 12.00 the rider asked for and not a FULL_REFUND.

The rider's establishment rests on unimpaired evidence. The trace carries 207 fixes at a 10-second interval with 100% coverage, no gaps and a maximum gap of 0 seconds, so limbs (a) to (c) of POL-RD-07 do not fire, no independent corroboration is required of the rider, and neither POL-RD-10(3) nor the POL-GEN-02 confidence cap is engaged. Every artifact the rider relies on carries weight 1.0.

The rider's own claim history does not raise the bar she must clear: rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 1, well below the 4-claim trigger in POL-RD-08, so the additional-corroboration requirement for low-value excess does not apply to a claim that is otherwise proven. Under POL-GEN-01 the remaining fields on the rider profile - rating, account age, lifetime trips, prior disputes - are context only and cannot be used to discount her account of this trip.

The rider does not overreach for the POL-RD-06 uplift, and says so on the record: the driver's trailing-90-day figures are deviation_flags_90d 0 over completed_trips_90d 511, so no repeat pattern is established, no full-refund uplift follows from it and no conduct referral is sought. The rider's monetary remedy is the POL-RD-02 partial - the arithmetic figure of 8.00 - and nothing more.

claims.text: The rider asked for this detour herself. MSG-00109-001 in the chat log was sent by RIDER at 18:22:06, roughly a minute after the meter started at 18:21:10, and reads 'hi can stop at jurong point first? need to grab something 5 min'; the platform resolved that message to a waypoint_hint of Jurong Point PHV Pickup Point, 1 Jurong West Central 2 (VEN-JURONG-POINT). That satisfies every limb of POL-RD-04: the instruction comes from the rider, it is timestamped before the vehicle left the optimal corridor rather than more than three minutes after, and it names a place specifically enough to act on. The driver accepted it thirteen seconds later with 'ok can, i wait at the phv pickup point'.

The trace corroborates the requested stop, so POL-RD-04's corroboration test is run and passed rather than undecidable. EV-GPS-00109 is unbroken 10-second telemetry with 100% coverage, 207 fixes and max_gap_sec of 0.0, and its admissibility assessment records the vehicle stationary 38 m from the Jurong Point PHV pickup point named in the rider's own message for 366 seconds, well inside the 200 m corroboration radius the clause requires. The same trace lists a 0.0 km/h speed sample among its distinct speeds, which is a vehicle waiting at a pickup point, not a vehicle driving past one.

Because the detour was rider-caused, the excess distance between leaving and rejoining the optimal corridor is excluded before POL-RD-01 and POL-RD-02 are applied, as POL-RD-04 expressly directs. The derived deviation block measures 7.36 km of excess at 115.00% of an optimal of 6.4 km, but that block is itself computed on the raw trace total (trace_distance_km 13.76 against optimal_distance_km 6.4) and takes no account of the exclusion the clause requires. Once the rider-requested Jurong Point leg is removed, the deviation gate in POL-RD-01 is not met and no POL-RD-02 recomputation runs.

No residual excess above the POL-RD-01 threshold is shown on this record. The 7.36 km and 115.00% figures are unadjusted totals; nothing in the derived block, the trip record or the fare breakdown isolates a post-exclusion excess, and under POL-RD-08 the rider carries the burden of proving an excess measured after the rider-caused leg comes out. A materiality figure computed before the adjustment the governing clause mandates cannot discharge that burden.

The POL-RD-06 profile check comes back clean and no uplift or referral is available on it. Even if the judge treats a material deviation as recorded, driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 511, a ratio of 0.00, far below the 0.05 with at least 40 completed trips that POL-RD-06 requires before a pattern is established. No pattern means no limb (a) tilt of a balanced record, no limb (b) uplift of the contested SGD 21.32 to a FULL_REFUND, and no limb (c) conduct referral. The lifetime counter prior_deviation_flags is not the trailing-90-day field the clause names and cannot be substituted for it.

The driver is owed compensation for distance the platform never billed. fare_breakdown.distance_charged_km is 9.60 while the governing gps_trace.trace_distance_km is 13.76, a shortfall of 4.16 km that exceeds the 1.0 km gate in POL-RD-04's compensation limb. At SGD 0.75 per unbilled kilometre that is 3.12, rounded up to the nearest SGD 0.05 as SGD 3.15, comfortably inside the SGD 15.00 per-trip cap. The payments artifact flags the shortfall itself as a substantive POL-RD-04 finding, not a cross-source data error.

No traffic advisory exists for this trip and the driver does not need one: EV-ADVIS-00109-01 is MISSING from the pool, carries no payload, and has admissibility weight 0.0 with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, so no POL-RD-03 closure exoneration is asserted or available. The absence is citable and it is the platform's own assessment that 'the detour is explained by the rider's own instruction, not by any road condition' — which is precisely the POL-RD-04 route the driver relies on.

There is no pass-through money to correct on top. The fare breakdown carries no ERP gantries and erp_lines total 0.00, no tolls, an airport surcharge of 0.00 on a trip that neither originates nor ends at an airport, no promo discount and no waiting-time fee, so POL-RD-09 gives the rider nothing to add to the contested amount. The only contested money is the distance and time charge on the trip the rider herself asked to be extended.

On the rider's claim the present state stands, and the outcome this case produces is compensation to the driver. fare_breakdown.payment_status is CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd is 0.00; with POL-RD-04 exonerating the detour there is no POL-RD-02 recomputation to displace that charge, and under POL-GEN-03 NO_ACTION on a rider-filed dispute leaves the charge exactly as it is rather than restoring or increasing it. The ruling should therefore be DRIVER_COMPENSATION of SGD 3.15, with amount_sgd carrying that same figure, no refund to the rider, and no referral, since POL-RD-06(c) is not triggered.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and the driver: the GPS trace for TRP-00109 is clean — 207 fixes at 10-second intervals, 100% coverage, no gaps — and the trip record, trace and fare breakdown all carry the same trip ID and the same 18:21:10 start, so the trip itself is not in doubt. On the raw figures the vehicle drove 13.76 km (the trace figure, which POL-RD-01 makes governing) against a booked optimal of 6.4 km, an excess of 7.36 km / 115%, material on its face.

The rider's refund claim fails, and the driver is right about why. The chat log carries the rider's own message MSG-00109-001 at 18:22:06 — 'hi can stop at jurong point first? need to grab something 5 min' — resolved by the platform to the Jurong Point PHV Pickup Point waypoint, and the driver accepted 25 seconds later. The GPS trace corroborates it: the vehicle was stationary 38 m from that waypoint for 366 seconds, inside the 200 m radius POL-RD-04 requires, and its furthest point from the start (7,086 m) is consistent with reaching Jurong Point. Jurong Point sits roughly 7 km west of the Clementi–Bukit Batok optimal corridor, so the requested stop is what produced the excess; POL-RD-04 excludes that stretch before POL-RD-01 and POL-RD-02 run, no residual deviation survives the exclusion, and the rider's $21.32 charge stands (payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00). The rider's argument that the record contains no measured post-exclusion excess is rejected: the requested stop is a westward excursion off the whole optimal corridor, and it accounts for the excess. The $8.00 recomputed-fare figure the rider's advocate cites would only arise if the deviation stood; it does not, so no partial refund is due.

The driver is owed money. The fare breakdown bills distance_charged_km 9.6 against the trace's 13.76 km — 4.16 km unbilled, above the 1.0 km gate in POL-RD-04's compensation limb. At $0.75 per unbilled kilometre that is $3.12, rounded up to $3.15, inside the $15.00 per-trip cap. The platform's own assessment of the fare artifact treats this shortfall as a substantive POL-RD-04 finding rather than a cross-source conflict, and it is the figure this ruling moves.

The POL-RD-06 check is clean: deviation_flags_90d is 0 over completed_trips_90d of 511, so no repeat pattern, no full-refund uplift and no conduct referral follow — the lifetime prior_deviation_flags counter is not the field the clause names and was not used. POL-RD-09 adds nothing: ERP totals 0.00, there are no tolls, no airport surcharge and no promo or waiting-time lines, so there is no pass-through correction. The traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-00109-01 is MISSING (weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT) and provides no closure exoneration, but none is needed on this record. Every artifact carrying this ruling — the trip record, GPS trace, chat log and fare breakdown — is at weight 1.0, so the confidence is not discounted.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider: your trip ran 13.76 km on the GPS trace (the governing field) against a booked optimal of 6.4 km — an excess of 7.36 km, or 115%. Normally that would be refundable. It is not here, because you asked for it. Your message at 18:22:06, one minute after the meter started, read 'hi can stop at jurong point first? need to grab something 5 min', and the platform saved Jurong Point PHV Pickup Point as the message's waypoint. The driver agreed at 18:22:31. The trace shows the car standing 38 m from that waypoint for 366 seconds — about six minutes, matching the driver's account — and the furthest point the car reached from your pickup, 7.09 km, is the distance to Jurong Point, so the route was Clementi → Jurong Point → Bukit Batok. POL-RD-04 excludes the distance between leaving and rejoining the optimal corridor, and here that is the whole of the 7.36 km excess. No deviation therefore stands, and the $21.32 charge stays: the $12.00 you contested is not refunded. Your argument that no separate post-exclusion figure appears in the file is noted but rejected — the exclusion is run on the artifacts themselves (the message, its stored waypoint, and the trace's own path), and on that path nothing is left over. The $21.32 charged_total and the $13.32 recomputed fare are therefore not used, because POL-RD-02 never runs.

To the driver: for the same reason the distance and time charges stand. Separately, the fare breakdown billed 9.60 km while the trace records 13.76 km driven, so 4.16 km went unpaid. POL-RD-04 pays SGD 0.75 per unbilled kilometre: 4.16 × 0.75 = $3.12, rounded up to $3.15, well under the $15.00 per-trip cap. The ruling orders $3.15 to you, and that same figure is recorded as the amount the ruling moves.

For both: no traffic advisory covers this trip — the advisory artifact is missing, weight 0.0, which is noted but exonerates nothing, so POL-RD-03 gives no relief. There are no ERP, toll or airport-surcharge lines on the fare breakdown, so no pass-through correction arises under POL-RD-09. On the driver's profile, deviation_flags_90d is 0 over 511 completed trips in 90 days, so no repeat-deviation pattern is established and no driver-conduct referral is made. The rider's claim history (1 deviation claim in 60 days) does not trigger the extra-corroboration rule and did not affect the outcome. The trace is unimpaired (207 fixes, 10-second interval, no gaps), so nothing escalates. Every artifact that decides this case carries weight 1.0, so the confidence cap is 1.0; confidence is 0.9.

Both of you, here is what the record shows and how it is resolved.

RIDER — the detour you complain of was your own request. The in-app chat log (EV-CHAT-00109) shows you sent 'hi can stop at jurong point first? need to grab something 5 min' at 18:22:06, about a minute after the trip began, and the driver agreed thirteen seconds later. The GPS trace (EV-GPS-00109) places the vehicle stationary 38 m from the Jurong Point PHV pickup point (the waypoint_hint the platform resolved from your own message) for 366 seconds — exactly the 200 m corroboration POL-RD-04 requires. Because the additional stop was your instruction, POL-RD-04 excludes the excess distance of that leg before POL-RD-01 and POL-RD-02 are applied. What remains after that exclusion is the ordinary Clementi-to-Bukit-Batok run, which does not clear POL-RD-01's gates (more than 0.8 km AND more than 20% over the 6.4 km optimal). The figures on the trace — 13.76 km driven, 7.36 km (115%) over the 6.4 km optimal — are the UNADJUSTED totals, not the post-exclusion excess. No deviation stands, so no fare refund is due and POL-RD-02 is never run. Your argument that the driver failed to isolate the excludable portion is answered on the evidence: the waypoint you named lies well off the Clementi–Bukit Batok corridor, you asked for it 'first', and the trace shows the vehicle went there and waited; on this record the whole excess is the Jurong Point excursion. Your alternative claims that the trace governs the measurement (accepted), that POL-RD-05 and POL-RD-12 give the driver no new baseline (accepted — pickup/dropoff were not amended and the vehicle is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL), and that POL-RD-11 does not apply because the fare is METERED with quoted_fare_sgd null (accepted) leave the outcome unchanged; your claim for an SGD 8.00 part-refund assumes a deviation that does not survive POL-RD-04.

DRIVER — the fare ledger (EV-FARE-00109) billed the rider for 9.60 km while the governing GPS trace (EV-GPS-00109) records 13.76 km, a shortfall of 4.16 km, which exceeds the 1.0 km gate in POL-RD-04's compensation limb. At SGD 0.75 per unbilled kilometre that is SGD 3.12, rounded UP to SGD 3.15 and well within the SGD 15.00 cap. The POL-RD-06 driver-profile check comes back clean — deviation_flags_90d 0 over completed_trips_90d 511 — so no repeat pattern exists and no full-refund uplift or driver-conduct referral (POL-RD-06(c)) arises; the lifetime prior_deviation_flags counter is not the field that clause names and was not used.

Figures used: charged_total SGD 21.32 (left standing, not refunded); trace distance 13.76 km; billed distance 9.60 km; unbilled 4.16 km; rate SGD 0.75/km; compensation SGD 3.15. There is no ERP, toll, surcharge, promo or waiting-time line to correct under POL-RD-09, and the traffic-advisory artifact is absent (EV-ADVIS-00109-01, weight 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT), so no POL-RD-03 closure exoneration arises and nothing is carried by it. The trace is unimpaired (207 fixes, 10 s interval, 100% coverage, max gap 0 s) so POL-RD-07 creates no corroboration gap and POL-RD-10 does not fire. Every artifact that carries the deciding facts — the chat log, the GPS trace and the fare breakdown — is at weight 1.0, so nothing is down-weighted. On a DRIVER_COMPENSATION ruling amount_sgd carries the same figure as the driver payment, and the rider's own charge stands as NO_ACTION. No escalation is required and no clause produces a referral.

ruling.explanation:
Rider and driver — this is a route-deviation dispute over trip TRP-00109 (Clementi MRT to Bukit Batok MRT), charged at SGD 21.32. The outcome is DRIVER_COMPENSATION of SGD 3.15.

1. The deviation the rider measures is real on the raw trace, but it is rider-caused. The GPS trace records 13.76 km driven against a 6.4 km booked optimal — an excess of 7.36 km, 115%, which clears both POL-RD-01 gates and is material (trace-derived status 'material'). On that alone the rider's arithmetic would be a PARTIAL_REFUND: charged_total 21.32 less a recomputed fare of 13.32 (base 3.80 + 0.75 x 6.4 km + 0.28 x 14.0 min, surge multiplier 1.0 read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier, + 0.80 platform fee), giving 8.00, above the 0.50 de minimis and below the 90% full-refund share. That is the figure the rider asks me to award.

2. POL-RD-04 displaces it. The chat log (EV-CHAT-00109) shows MSG-00109-001, sent by the RIDER at 18:22:06 — about a minute after the trip started at 18:21:10, well inside the 3-minute window — reading 'hi can stop at jurong point first? need to grab something 5 min', which the platform resolved to a specific place, the Jurong Point PHV Pickup Point (VEN-JURONG-POINT) carried on the message's waypoint_hint. The driver accepted 25 seconds later. The corroboration limb is satisfied on the field the clause requires: the clean 10-second, 207-fix, zero-gap trace puts the vehicle stationary 38 m from that waypoint for 366 seconds, inside the 200 m radius. Every limb of POL-RD-04 passes, the clause is available (not undecidable), and the excess attributable to the requested Jurong Point stop is excluded before POL-RD-01 and POL-RD-02 run. The booked optimal runs Clementi Road to Bukit Batok East Ave 3; Jurong Point lies off that corridor in the opposite direction, so the whole of the 7.36 km excess is attributable to the stop the rider asked for. No deviation survives the exclusion and no distance-or-time refund is due. The rider's POL-RD-01, POL-RD-02 and POL-RD-08 claims all fail at this point — the raw excess they measure is the unadjusted figure the clause requires me to adjust — and her 8.00 claim is rejected.

3. The driver is owed for distance the platform never billed. fare_breakdown.distance_charged_km is 9.60 against the trace's 13.76 km — a shortfall of 4.16 km, above the 1.0 km gate in POL-RD-04's compensation limb. At SGD 0.75 per unbilled kilometre that is 3.12, rounded UP to SGD 3.15, inside the SGD 15.00 per-trip cap. That limb is granted.

4. Everything else falls away. EV-ADVIS-00109-01 is MISSING (no payload, weight 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT); its absence carries no fact and no POL-RD-03 closure exoneration is asserted or available — the rider's point that the driver has no road-condition answer is correct and does not help her. The fare breakdown carries no ERP gantries, no tolls, zero airport surcharge, no promo and no waiting-time fee, so POL-RD-09 gives nothing to either side. The driver's profile shows no repeat pattern (deviation_flags_90d 0 over completed_trips_90d 511, a ratio of 0.00, far below the 0.05 / 40-trip test), so no POL-RD-06 limb (a) tilt, no limb (b) uplift to FULL_REFUND and no limb (c) conduct referral — both advocates agree on this and I confirm it. The profile fields raised in argument (rider rating, account age, lifetime trips, prior disputes; driver prior_deviation_flags) are context-only under POL-GEN-01 and are correctly not used as grounds by either side; no claim was discarded for that reason. POL-RD-05 and POL-RD-12 do not apply (no amendment timestamps and amended_optimal_distance_km null; vehicle_type RYDE_X not RYDE_POOL). The trace is unimpaired under POL-RD-07(a)-(c) (max gap 0 s, sampling 10 s, no jumps), so no corroboration requirement or confidence cap arises from impairment, and the only sub-1.0 artifact in the pool is the missing advisory, which carries no fact. No POL-RD-10 trigger fires: identifiers and pickup timestamps match, no timestamp disagreement, no missing field behind an invoked exculpatory clause, no unmatched charge line, and no comparable-strength contradiction — the GPS corroborates the rider's own request rather than contradicting it.

5. Under POL-GEN-03 a DRIVER_COMPENSATION ruling carries the same figure in amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd: SGD 3.15. The rider's charge stands as billed (payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00). Figures used: charged_total 21.32; recomputed fare 13.32; billed distance 9.60 km; trace distance 13.76 km; shortfall 4.16 km; 4.16 x 0.75 = 3.12 rounded up to 3.15. No clause produces a referral on these facts.
